title: Chapter 15: Testing, Debugging, and Logging
description: Create layered evidence for correctness and diagnosis. Learners design deterministic unit, integration, and journey tests; use JUnit assertions and parameterized cases; choose fakes or mocks at genuine boundaries; debug from a minimal reproduction and explicit hypothesis; and design logs, metrics, and traces that distinguish failures without duplicating noise or leaking secrets.

exercises.instructionMarkdown: What does line coverage fail to prove?
choices: That assertions test the right behavior
hints: Coverage tools only record that a line executed; they cannot tell you whether the assertions that ran actually validate the right behavior.

exercises.title: JUnit lifecycle, assertions, parameterized tests, and exceptions: concept check
choices: To fail the test if the expected failure does not occur
To retry the operation until no exception is thrown
hints: assertThrows runs the lambda and fails the test automatically if the expected exception type is never thrown, unlike a manual try/catch that can silently pass.

exercises.instructionMarkdown: Does a mock JDBC connection prove SQL correctness?
choices: No; a real database integration test is needed
hints: A mocked Connection only returns whatever stubbed answers you configure; it never actually parses or executes SQL against a real schema.

lessons.title: Reproduction, hypotheses, breakpoints, stepping, and thread dumps

exercises.title: Reproduction, hypotheses, breakpoints, stepping, and thread dumps: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: What is a useful debugging hypothesis?
choices: A conclusion based only on compilation
A specific explanation that an observation can disprove
A random edit that might help
hints: A useful hypothesis names a specific mechanism, such as an off-by-one loop bound, that a single targeted observation could prove false.

lessons.title: Structured logging, levels, correlation, metrics, and traces

exercises.title: Structured logging, levels, correlation, metrics, and traces: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Why avoid user IDs as metric labels?
choices: Unbounded cardinality can overload metric storage
Metric labels are limited to a single fixed value at compile time
High-cardinality labels only affect log file size, not the metrics backend
hints: Each distinct label value creates a new time series in most metrics backends, so unbounded values like user IDs can multiply storage and query cost.

exercises.title: Testing, Debugging, and Logging: professional judgment
exercises.instructionMarkdown: A mock-heavy suite passes while real SQL fails. What evidence is missing?
choices: Integration tests against the chosen database
More mock verifications of the same calls
A longer sleep in unit tests

exercises.title: Chapter 15 implementation lab: diagnostic
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Implement `diagnostic`. Return exactly expected=<expected>, actual=<actual> using the two integer values. Write the precondition and boundary table first, keep the method deterministic, and do not print.

Use the exact punctuation shown; no extra whitespace or line endings.
hints: Match the exact literal text 'expected=' and ', actual=' with no extra spaces or punctuation.
Check zero and negative values for both parameters before submitting, since the format must hold for every integer.

exercises.title: An assertion must execute without JVM flags
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Repair the check so it does not rely on Java's disabled-by-default assert statement, and the program writes exactly `true`. Keep the same failed-flag pattern and explain why assert silently does nothing without the -ea flag while an explicit throw does not, rather than hard-coding the print statement. Output tests verify the printed result; confirming the check truly executes requires reading the source.
hints: Replace the disabled-by-default assert statement with an explicit check that throws AssertionError.

exercises.title: Validated monthly expense report
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Implement MonthlyReport.run(String input). Each nonblank line contains date|cents. Trim fields. Date must have ASCII yyyy-MM-dd shape and be a valid LocalDate in years 0001..9999; cents must be a positive int. Reject bad records and count ERRORS. Group accepted amounts by YearMonth and sum into long. Output months in ascending order as yyyy-MM=total, followed by ERRORS=<count>. Empty input returns ERRORS=0. Use explicit parsing, preserve valid records after errors, and do not use the real current date. At most 10000 input lines are supplied; this bounds total amounts.
hints: Parse and validate all fields before mutating state. Split with a negative limit when empty fields must be preserved.
Choose collections according to identity and ordering requirements. Build output lines and join them with a newline.
